title: Inessive forms before plural nouns
summary: Match näissä, noissa, or niissä with a supplied plural inessive noun.
objectives: Place a plural inessive demonstrative before its noun.
Match plural number and inessive case.
Keep the supplied plural noun form unchanged.

sections.title: See the pattern
paragraphs: Before a plural inessive noun, use näissä, noissa, or niissä: näissä kirjoissa, noissa laukuissa, niissä taloissa.
The demonstrative and noun match in both case and plural number.

sections.title: Use one clear decision
paragraphs: The complete noun form is supplied so the learner does not have to derive a hidden plural stem.
The target decision is the demonstrative form only.

steps: Avaimet: the complete plural form is supplied.
näissä: learned inessive form of nämä.
laukuissa: the complete non-target noun form is supplied.

examples.english: Books are in those bags over there.
steps: Kirjat: the complete plural form is supplied.
noissa: learned inessive form of nuo.
laukuissa: the complete non-target noun form is supplied.
Avaimet: the complete plural form is supplied.
niissä: learned inessive form of ne.
autoissa: the complete non-target noun form is supplied.

commonMistakes: Do not use singular tässä with a plural inessive noun.
Do not use nominative nämä before an inessive noun.
Do not reconstruct or change the supplied plural noun form.

Correct. Näissä matches laukuissa in inessive case and plural number.
“nämä” is a plural nominative form for referents near the speaker; use “näissä”, the plural inessive form linked to nämä.
“noissa” is the plural inessive form linked to nuo; use “näissä”, the plural inessive form linked to nämä.
“Avaimet ovat näissä laukussa.” changes the supplied form or word order. The required sentence is “Avaimet ovat näissä laukuissa.”: Näissä matches laukuissa in inessive case and plural number.
